title: Day 31 · Week 4, Day 3 — Parents: the second adult — what a father's involvement measurably does, the smoke in the house, and the one father in ten who gets depressed
summary: The father-involvement evidence promised on Episode Zero and Day 28, read honestly. Your baby is about 0.4 mm, gathering the cardiogenic field that becomes the heart, a day or two from the neural plate. Why nearly all the evidence is observational and what that means. The ECLS-B cohort (5,404 US women): involved partners went with 1.5× the odds of first-trimester prenatal care, and a suggestive (p = 0.09) 36% greater cut in smoking. The 2010 English national maternity survey (4,616 women): over half of fathers at the test and at one or more checks, nearly all at scans and labour, three quarters on paternity leave, and engagement linked to earlier first contact, dating scans, classes and breastfeeding, with leave linked to maternal wellbeing at three months. Florida birth records and the honest limits of 'father absent on the birth certificate'. The AAP's 2016 clinical report. The active ingredients from a 120-publication meta-analysis — emotional closeness, support of both kinds, communication, relationship satisfaction, less conflict — and the reciprocal-support Delphi study. Secondhand smoke (stillbirth OR 1.23 from a 1-in-175 baseline; malformations OR 1.13) and the Cochrane nicotine-replacement evidence (RR 1.55, 133 trials). Then the father: about 10% depressed between the first trimester and the first year, 13.6% in the first trimester; paternal postnatal depression roughly doubling child behaviour problems at 3.5 years (ALSPAC), two thirds of it through maternal mood and couple conflict.
action: Find the date of the first prenatal visit booked on Day 28 and put it in your own calendar as a fixed, protected block; tell your partner you'll be there. If you smoke, this outranks it: set a quit date within two weeks and buy nicotine patches or gum today.
